bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Dependence on two principal suppliers/OEMs — The Board's Report describes the business as trading and distribution of iron and steel products primarily sourced from Tata Steel and tractors of John Deere India, so the revenue base rests on continuation of two principal relationships and their commercial terms.
- Single-state geographic concentration in Bihar — The Board's Report states the trading and distribution business is conducted in the state of Bihar, and the MD&A calls Bihar the principal geography of operations, so demand, competition and policy exposure are concentrated in one state economy.
- Commodity-price cyclicality across steel and crude-linked inputs — The MD&A notes base-metal prices including iron ore and steel saw a moderate cyclical recovery only in the latter half of the year and crude oil ranged between USD 70 and USD 85 per barrel; a trading-led model with PVC and freight inputs is exposed to those price swings.
- Reliance on the government capital-expenditure cycle for end demand — The MD&A attributes downstream demand for steel, building materials and farm mechanisation to public capex, the Gati Shakti Master Plan, the National Infrastructure Pipeline, PLI schemes and the Jal Jeevan Mission, and Bihar demand to a record railway allocation and rural-bridge and housing programmes; any moderation in those outlays flows straight into the Company's core verticals.
- Global geopolitical and trade-policy volatility — The MD&A frames calendar 2025 as cautious resilience amid persistent geopolitical tensions and evolving trade-policy realignments, which affect steel trade flows, import competition and input costs.
- Industry capacity expansion outrunning consumption — The MD&A records installed Indian steel capacity crossing 220 MTPA against a National Steel Policy target of 300 MTPA by 2030, while finished steel consumption is around 164 million tonnes, implying a supply-led market whose pricing can compress distributor economics.

business.body: Incorporated in 1994 and headquartered in Patna, Bihar, the Company operates across five complementary verticals: trading and distribution of iron and steel products sourced primarily from Tata Steel Limited; authorised distribution of John Deere India tractors, tractor engines and spare parts across Bihar; manufacture of PVC pipes under the BMW Polytube brand; fabrication of pre-engineered buildings and RDSO-approved railway girders from its Purnea facility; and rental of construction equipment. Its customers are builders, contractors, infrastructure and housing developers, farmers and industrial buyers within Bihar, served through a dealer-led distribution model. Management aggregates all activities into a single operating segment under Ind AS 108, with the bulk of business derived from iron and steel trading and distribution and the other verticals providing complementary contributions.

- **PVC pipes manufacturing:** BMW Polytube
- **Fabrication:** Pre-Engineered Buildings (PEBs), Railway girders (RDSO-approved)
- **Equipment rental:** Construction equipment on rent

outlook.body:
- The Company states a Dividend Distribution Policy that endeavours for fairness, consistency and sustainability while distributing profits to Members, with the policy published on the Company's website. Capital-structure policy during the year was oriented to deleveraging: the movement in borrowings, comprising repayment of long-term borrowings and a reduction in working-capital borrowings, was effected primarily out of the proceeds of the initial public offer, and the Company reports no non-cash changes in liabilities arising from financing activities. Governance overlays on capital allocation include Audit Committee omnibus and quarterly review of related-party transactions (with nothing to report in Form AOC-2 for FY 2025-26), a Related Party Transaction Policy and a Whistle Blower Policy with direct access to the Chairman of the Audit Committee, and a statement that no significant or material orders were passed by regulators or courts that would impact going-concern status or future operations.
- Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report under Regulation 34(2)(f) of the SEBI Listing Regulations is not applicable to the Company for FY 2025-26, so no BRSR-based sustainability metrics or targets are disclosed.
- CSR provisions under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013 apply to the Company; a Board-approved CSR Policy recommended by the CSR Committee is in place and published on the Company's website, with the year's CSR initiatives set out in Annexure-I of the Board's Report.
- Nomination and Remuneration Policy lays down criteria for appointment of Directors, KMP and Senior Management and includes a framework on Board diversity.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The routed sections disclose no named capacity-addition, greenfield or brownfield capex project with a commissioning, completion or ramp timeline. The Board's Report records that the Company remains engaged in trading and distribution of iron and steel products sourced primarily from Tata Steel and tractors of John Deere India in the state of Bihar, together with manufacturing of PVC pipes and pre-engineered buildings and railway girders, and states expressly that there was no change in the business activities of the Company during the financial year. The material corporate development of the year was structural rather than physical: the Company issued equity shares through an Initial Public Offer and its shares were listed on the National Stock Exchange of India Limited and BSE Limited with effect from October 1, 2025. The Company had no subsidiary, associate or joint venture company as on March 31, 2026, and none was acquired or ceased during the year, so no expansion occurred through the corporate-structure route either.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Global macro backdrop described as cautious resilience: IMF-estimated global growth of around 3.2 per cent for 2025, easing inflation and cautious rate normalisation by the US Federal Reserve, the ECB and the RBI.
- Commodity markets remained range-bound, with crude oil between USD 70 and USD 85 per barrel and base metals including iron ore and steel seeing a moderate cyclical recovery in the latter half on Asian replenishment demand; supply-chain stability improved meaningfully.
- India remained the fastest-growing major economy, with real GDP estimated to grow at 7.4 per cent in FY 2025-26 versus 6.5 per cent in FY 2024-25, and manufacturing and construction estimated to grow at around 7.00 per cent.
- Gross Fixed Capital Formation expanded an estimated 7.8 per cent on sustained public capex and a gradual revival in private investment; the Union Budget 2025-26 retained a capex outlay of approximately Rs.11.21 lakh crore with infrastructure outlay near 3.1 per cent of GDP.
- Gati Shakti Master Plan, the National Infrastructure Pipeline, PLI schemes across fourteen sectors and the Jal Jeevan Mission collectively created broad-based downstream demand for steel, building materials and farm mechanisation - all core verticals of the Company.
- Bihar, the Company's principal geography, is among the fastest-growing states: GSDP for FY 2025-26 projected at approximately Rs.10.97 lakh crore at current prices, growing around 22 per cent year-on-year, with a CAGR of 11.42 per cent between FY 2015-16 and FY 2025-26.
- Bihar-specific spending catalysts: a record railway-budget allocation of Rs.10,066 crore in FY 2025-26, greenfield airports at Sultanganj and Raxaul, the Mukhyamantri Gramin Setu Yojana proposing 700 rural bridges, and continued thrust on rural electrification, irrigation and housing.
- Management links those state-level developments directly to a structural uptick in demand for TMT bars, structural steel, galvanised sheets, PVC pipes, pre-engineered buildings and farm mechanisation - the precise product categories the Company services.
- Indian steel demand backdrop: crude steel output grew over 10.7 per cent year-on-year to approximately 168.4 million tonnes in FY 2025-26, finished steel consumption reached around 164 million tonnes (up 7-8 per cent), and installed capacity crossed 220 MTPA against the National Steel Policy target of 300 MTPA by 2030.

open.item: Scale up the core steel-distribution franchise by deepening dealer penetration across the untapped talukas of Bihar in FY 2026-27.
Build order-book momentum in pre-engineered buildings and railway girders, leveraging the Purnea facility's RDSO accreditation.
Selectively scale the PVC-pipes business during FY 2026-27.
Deploy the strengthened balance sheet towards working-capital efficiency, debtor-cycle management and prudent capital expenditure.
Strengthen governance, investor communication and ESG disclosures consistent with newly listed status.
Fully deploy the remaining IPO proceeds into business operations, with return on net worth expected to normalise progressively as that deployment completes.
Management flags heavy concentration of steel revenue on a single principal supplier, where any supply disruption or change in commercial or distribution terms could affect the trading business.
Management flags geographic concentration of operations in Bihar and dependence on the monsoon and farm incomes for the tractor distribution business.
